seats._percentile_why: the soma detector accepted for the Issue 013 two-soma gate, at the settings its own 54-point sweep chose. Reused rather than retuned so seats are found by a measurement fixed before this approach existed.
seats._maximum_step_px_why: a soma moves slowly between frames; 12 px is also the minimum separation the accepted gate uses to call two cores distinct, so a seat cannot step onto its neighbour.
seats._maximum_valley_ratio_why: measured, not chosen: over all 229 multi-soma components in the accepted base the bottleneck between two somas is at most 0.366 of the weaker soma at the 95th percentile, and the median is 0.124. A cut at 0.5 admits every separation the movie actually contains with margin.
seats._surrender_fraction_why: Jamie, 2026-08-19: 'a takeover can only happen on the full region not just a small part (otherwise cells slowly eat at eachother)'. A defender still standing on more than a tenth of its own body has not lost a contest, so the claim is refused.
seats._dim_why: rule D only. A dim cell has no absolute brightness to be found by, so it is found by the drop around it: a local maximum survives when the highest saddle joining it to a brighter maximum lies below half its own height. The 0.5 cut is the same measured number as the valley test.
seats._prior_marker_clearance_why: rule B only. A name whose body wraps another cell's soma is wearing that soma, not neighbouring it, and the seat exists to take it back. Only ground at least this far from every soma in the object counts as a neighbour holding its own.
